title: Cap. XIV / Man. Post. Cap. I: Manuscriptum posterius title; LICEAT address; common heads
pass_a_gloss: THE LATER MANUSCRIPT, THAT IS, AN EXAMINATION of a singular Tractate, On original sin, in which it is demonstrated that the first sin of the first man is imputed to all men, opposed to Theses on the state of fallen man before grace, disputed at Saumur on the 16th of March in the year 1640 under the presidency of Josue Placeus, Professor of Sacred Theology in the Academy of Saumur. CHAPTER I. Heads of doctrine on Original Sin concerning which we agree among ourselves. Let it be permitted me, I ask, reverend Sir, to address and speak to you just as if the matter were being handled in conversation face to face: for so, as I hope, your presence, as if meeting my eyes, will arouse me who am sluggish, and will compose me to greater reverence toward you. You indeed by your singular prudence wished to fortify for yourself a way to establishing the state of the controversy, having first laid down those things concerning which we agree among ourselves. Which counsel of yours I greatly approve; but (which I would wish said with your good leave) you have seemed to me to have performed neither with enough accuracy and clearness. Suffer therefore that I do both by your example briefly indeed, yet so that from this our friendly conference all confusion, if it can be done, may be removed, all ambiguity.
pass_b_english: THE LATER MANUSCRIPT, that is, an Examination of a singular tractate On original sin, which argues that the first man's first sin is imputed to all, set against Theses on the state of fallen man before grace, disputed at Saumur on 16 March 1640 under Josue de la Place, professor of theology there. Chapter I. Heads of doctrine on original sin on which we agree. Let me address you, reverend Sir, as if we spoke face to face: so your presence before my eyes may wake my dullness and tune me to deeper reverence. By your singular prudence you wished to clear the state of the question by first laying down what we hold in common. I much approve that plan; yet (with your leave) you seem to me to have done neither part with enough care and clearness. Allow me therefore to do both after your example—briefly, yet so that from this friendly conference every confusion and ambiguity may, if possible, be cleared away.
source_text: MANUSCRIPTUM POSTERIUS, HOC EST, EXAMEN Tractatus singularis, De peccato originis, in quo demonstratur primum primi hominis peccatum omnibus hominibus imputari, oppositi Thesibus de statu hominis lapsi ante gratiam, disputatis Salmurii die 16. Martii An. 1640. sub Praesidio Josue Placei S. Theologiae Professoris in Academia Salmuriensi. CAPUT I. Capita doctrinae de Peccato originali de quibus inter nos convenit. LICEAT mihi, quaeso, Vir reverende, te, perinde ac si coram sermone res ageretur, compellare et alloqui: Sic enim, uti spero, tua, velut oculis meis obversantis praesentia me torpentem excitabit, et ad tui majorem reverentiam componet. Tu quidem pro tua singulari prudentia voluisti tibi viam ad statum controversiae constituendum munire, praestratis iis de quibus inter nos convenit. Quod tuum consilium valde probo; sed (quod cum tua bona venia dictum velim) visus es mihi neutrum praestitisse satis accurate et enucleate. Patere igitur ut utrumque tuo exemplo faciam breviter quidem, sed ita tamen, ut ab hac nostra amica collatione omnis, si fieri possit, tollatur confusio, omnis ambiguitas.
